intro_html: Sausages and root vegetables roasted in one pan, and then the gravy gets made in that same pan using everything stuck to the bottom. No second pot, no gravy packet, no wasted flavor. It is a big, generous plate at 35 grams of protein and about $1.83 a bowl.
cost_closing_html: About $1.83 a bowl for a roast dinner with pan gravy. Two thirds of that is the sausage, so a sale on brats moves this number more than anything else you can do.
shop_smart: Sausage is two thirds of the cost. Everything else on the list combined is a small fraction of the total. Buy brats on sale, freeze them, and this recipe gets meaningfully cheaper.
Potatoes and carrots are the cheap bulk. Bagged potatoes and bagged carrots fill both pans for very little, and both keep for weeks.
Red onions cost more than yellow. They look prettier roasted, but if the board shows a gap, yellow onions do the identical job for less.
The gravy is butter, flour and broth. That is a small line on the cost list and it beats any jarred gravy you can buy.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into chunks, cut the carrots into thick batons, and cut the red onions into wedges.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, minced garlic, dried thyme, dried oregano, salt and black pepper, then spread them across two large sheet pans.
Nestle the bratwurst among the vegetables and roast until the sausages are browned and the vegetables are tender and caught at the edges.
Move the sausages and vegetables to a holding pan and keep them warm. Do not wash the roasting pan, because everything stuck to it is the gravy.
Set that pan across two burners, melt the butter in it, and scrape hard while it bubbles to lift all the browned bits.
Whisk in the flour and cook it for a minute, then pour in the beef broth in a steady stream while whisking until the gravy thickens.
Slice the sausages, combine them with the vegetables in your big pot, and pour the gravy over the top.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1. Divide that total by 14 and scoop the exact amount into each container, counting sausage slices so the protein lands even. Every bowl lands near 856 calories and 35 grams of protein.

head.description: Sausages roasted with potatoes, carrots and red onion, finished with a gravy made in the same pan. 14 servings, 856 calories, 35g protein, about $1.83 each.
head.keywords: one pan sausage bake, sausage and vegetable bake with gravy, roasted sausages and potatoes, onion gravy, budget meal prep
steps: Toss the chopped potatoes, carrots and red onion with olive oil, garlic, thyme, oregano, salt and pepper.
Spread the vegetables on sheet pans, nestle in the sausages, and roast at 425F until browned and tender.
Move the food to a holding pan and melt butter in the unwashed roasting pan, scraping up the browned bits.
Whisk in flour, then stream in the beef broth and whisk until the gravy thickens.
Slice the sausages, combine with the vegetables, and pour the gravy over.
